_comment: Settings for the traditional-song pipeline (tools/songs-*.mjs). Nothing here is duplicated in code: the scaffold, the builder, the validator and the two checks all read this file. Same split as the Tehilim pipeline — the machine owns every Hebrew character, the author writes English only.
_comment_families: Sefaria serves a different default version per corpus, and the default is not always one we may redistribute: asking for a Tanakh verse plainly returns the JPS Gender-Sensitive Edition under CC-BY-NC. So every family names its versions in preference order and the scaffold records the one it actually got. A family whose preferences all miss is an error, never a silent fallback to the default.

tanakh.label: Tanakh
en: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917)

siddur.label: Siddur
siddur._comment_order: Preference, not fallback: the scaffold walks this list and takes the first version that is both licensed and VOCALIZED. Daat leads because it is Public Domain, but it serves some zemirot unpointed, and an unpointed zemer is useless on a site that teaches reading — so the list must have somewhere to go next.
he: The Metsudah Siddur, Metsudah Publications, 1981 - HE
en: Translation based on the Metsudah linear siddur, by Avrohom Davis, 1981
Siddur Ashkenaz, trans. Sefaria Community Translation

_comment_licences: What we may redistribute. The site ships LICENSE-CONTENT (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), so a NonCommercial source is compatible, but a source with no stated licence is not something to bake into a public page. 'unknown' is absent on purpose.
_comment_categories: Drives the index cards and the section a song lands in. Order here is the order on the home page.

attribution.hebrew: Hebrew text from Sefaria, version and licence recorded per song in content/songs/source/.
attribution.english: English gloss lines authored for this site; the source translation is used as raw material only.
attribution.transliteration: Transliteration generated by this site's own engine (assets/translit.js).

readAs._comment: Vocalized Hebrew -> the transliteration a reader should say, for the words where the spelling and the reading part company. Keyed on the exact string as it comes out of the pinned edition.
